clue.text: Party to divorce case agreeing on involvement of redhead

indicators.note: involvement means being drawn inside, so the short piece is taken into the long legal term

blocks.note: a co-respondent is the third party named in a divorce for adultery
the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A divorce hearing where the other party turns out to be a redhead who goes along with everything.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase looks like the definition, but it supplies CO-RESPONDENT; adding a second R gives CORRESPONDENT, the definition being the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondent as an adjective means corresponding, matching or in accord with something, which is what agreeing describes.

clue.text: Workman in action

blocks.note: first meaning: a factory or skilled manual worker
second meaning: functioning, in force

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a labourer busy on the job, but the two halves are separate senses of one word, a noun and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An operative is a machine worker or artisan, and a rule or system that is operative is currently working and effective.

clue.text: Animal put out by the ear

indicators.note: going by the ear means judging only by what is heard, not by spelling

blocks.note: to put out someone is to fluster or unnerve them

explanation.surface: An animal is being thrown out of somewhere by its ear.
explanation.walkthrough: The ratel is the honey badger of Africa and India; its name is said like the verb meaning to unsettle.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel, or honey badger, is a fierce burrowing mammal of the weasel family, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Loud-mouth gets back to start riot

indicators.note: going back means running in the opposite direction, so this word is read right to left
the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept from riot

blocks.note: to net is to catch or get, so gets is nets
taken as written
first letter of riot

explanation.surface: A shouter is taken back to the beginning of a riot he started.
explanation.walkthrough: Stentor was the herald in the Iliad with a voice as loud as fifty men, hence stentorian.
explanation.definitionFit: A stentor is a person with a very powerful voice, after the Greek herald, so a loud-mouth in the literal sense.

clue.text: Letter sent to a remote station?

blocks.note: something sent has gone out
letters are post, the mail

explanation.surface: Mail being dispatched to a soldier at a distant frontier base.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words are taken in reverse order: what is sent comes first, then the letter. The question mark flags the loose 'post out' play.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a small military or trading station established far from the main settlement, a remote station exactly.

clue.text: Poor diet''s effects on banker

indicators.note: the effects of a poor diet are what it does to you, a change worked on these letters

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: The health consequences of bad eating on a city financier.
explanation.walkthrough: Banker usually means the bank, but here it is anyone who banks money; the apostrophe-s is just part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps money in a bank account is a depositor, so a banker in the sense of a person who banks savings.

clue.text: Informer trapping nothing in snare

indicators.note: trapping something means holding it inside, so the letters for nothing sit within the informer

blocks.note: a nose is slang for a police informer
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A police informer catches nothing in his trap.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a nose is a police informer, someone who sniffs things out.
explanation.definitionFit: A noose is a running loop of rope that tightens when pulled, the classic snare for catching animals.

clue.text: Say "when" at Buckingham Palace, for instance

definitions.note: describes the noun by the setting of such an event

blocks.note: to say is to state
a when is a time or occasion

explanation.surface: Telling a host when to stop pouring the drink, perhaps at a royal palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Saying when is what you do when someone pours you a drink; here it splits into say plus when. Buckingham Palace is the London residence of the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A state occasion is a formal ceremonial event of government or monarchy, such as a banquet held at the royal residence.

clue.text: Paper sign to produce factual programmes

blocks.note: a paper is a document
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A newspaper and a star sign are combined to create TV programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Documentaries are films or broadcasts presenting real events and facts, as opposed to fiction or drama.

clue.text: Use therapy

blocks.note: first meaning: the way something is handled or dealt with
second meaning: medical care given for an illness

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to use therapy, but both words are nouns naming the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: The way you handle an object is its treatment, and medical care for a condition is also called a course of treatment.

clue.text: Snap providing quiet hoot, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps marks the letters as only one possible form, so they may be rearranged

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction for quiet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soft owl call that might come out in a quick shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is a snapshot, an informal photograph taken quickly, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Dog track

blocks.note: first meaning: to follow someone closely, as a verb
second meaning: a path or the marks left behind

explanation.walkthrough: Dog track suggests a greyhound stadium, but dog is a verb meaning to follow persistently.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to follow or shadow them, and a trail is also a rough path or the scent left by an animal.

clue.text: What bride may want from leading theological writer

indicators.note: leading means at the front, so only the opening letter of theological is used

blocks.note: first letter of theological
Jean-Jacques Rousseau, the French philosopher and author

explanation.surface: A wedding wish list drawn from a prominent writer on religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Leading theological writer pretends to be one person; it is the first letter of one word plus a famous writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes, linen and household goods a bride collects for her marriage, something she would want ready.

clue.text: Show including one actor of renown

indicators.note: including means taking something in, so the number one goes inside the show's title

blocks.note: Oliver! is the Lionel Bart musical
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A stage show that features one famous actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver! is a long-running London stage musical based on Oliver Twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was among the most celebrated British stage and film actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Boyfriend getting girl doctor to change rota

indicators.note: to change the word means to alter its order, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Ina is a girl's name
MO is a medical officer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man gets his girlfriend, a doctor, to rearrange her shifts.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like the anagram signal, but it gives MO; change is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorato, from Italian, is a male lover or sweetheart, so a boyfriend.

clue.text: Birds following one with rodents

blocks.note: one of the birds just named: a tit
mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A flock of birds trailing after one bird accompanied by some rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: One refers back to the definition: one of the birds, singular, is a tit, and the rodents follow it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titmice is the full plural of titmouse, the old name for tits such as blue tits and great tits.

clue.text: Bring in a book of great consequence

blocks.note: to import goods is to bring them in
taken as written
NT is the New Testament, a book of the Bible

explanation.surface: Bringing in a weighty volume of real significance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something important matters a lot, so it is of great consequence; both phrases mean significant.

clue.text: Make about a thousand burn

indicators.note: about means around, so the verb's letters wrap round the number

blocks.note: to make is to create
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: An instruction to produce roughly a thousand of something that will burn.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate is to dispose of a corpse by burning it to ashes, so the verb means to burn.

clue.text: Self-centred people whose energy is set to run out?

blocks.clueFragment: whose energy is set to run out?
blocks.note: surface reading: people who are about to be exhausted

blocks.clueFragment: energy is set to run out
blocks.note: setter's reading: the word begins with E for energy followed by go, as if the E is ready to go

explanation.surface: Vain people whose stamina is about to give out.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the start of the answer as E GO IS: energy, then go, as if their E were set to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoists are people preoccupied with their own interests and importance, which is what self-centred describes.

clue.text: Monkey restrained by some low wall

indicators.note: something restrained is held in, so the animal is enclosed by the other word

blocks.note: some of something is part of it
an ape is a primate, loosely a monkey

explanation.surface: A monkey is held back by a short wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall along the edge of a roof, bridge or balcony.

clue.text: Aspire to be a suitor

blocks.note: first meaning: to lay claim to something, as in a claim to a throne
second meaning: to seek a woman's hand, an old sense

explanation.walkthrough: The modern sense is to make believe, which neither half uses; both rely on the older sense of making a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To pretend to something is to claim or aspire to it, and in older English it also meant to court or woo someone.

clue.text: American student getting nothing extra from new shop

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the shop's letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
O looks like zero
more is extra

explanation.surface: A US student gets nothing additional from a newly opened store.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagrammed shop comes first in the answer, though it is last in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a sophomore is a student in the second year of high school or college.

clue.text: Scheme to get one into flat

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the numeral is placed in the middle of the scheme

blocks.note: a scheme is a plan
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A plan to get someone into an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat suggests an apartment, which the scheme seems to be about; it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain is a flat expanse of land, and as an adjective plain also means level and smooth, without features.

clue.text: Nurse, for example, presenting vehicle to the Queen

blocks.note: a car is a vehicle
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A nurse hands over a car as a gift to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone who is ill or disabled, and a nurse is one such person who gives care.

clue.text: Tree in terraced arbour

indicators.note: in means contained within, so the letters lie inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A tree growing in a garden arbour on terraces.
explanation.definitionFit: The cedar is a large evergreen conifer, such as the cedar of Lebanon, so it is a tree.

clue.text: "One Meat Ball" sent back in Nebraska

definitions.note: names a place in Nebraska, so stands for a city there

indicators.note: sent back means returned the way it came, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: a means one
ham is a meat
O is round like a ball

explanation.surface: A diner order of a single meatball returned to the kitchen somewhere in Nebraska.
explanation.walkthrough: One Meat Ball is also a well-known old song title, hence the quotation marks.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha is the largest city in the US state of Nebraska, on the Missouri River.

clue.text: Duck captured by dissolute rakes

indicators.note: dissolute means loose and disordered, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: captured means held
taken as written

explanation.surface: A duck has been caught by a band of debauched rakes.
explanation.walkthrough: A rake is a dissolute man, so dissolute rakes seems a natural phrase; dissolute is the signal working on both words.
explanation.definitionFit: The sheldrake is a large, boldly coloured duck of coasts and estuaries, the male of the shelduck.

clue.text: Keep in mind ant that is wandering about, regardless of others

indicators.note: something wandering moves about at random, so these letters are jumbled
about means around, so the jumbled letters go round the phrase meaning keep in mind

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. is id est, that is
to consider something is to bear it in mind

explanation.surface: Bear in mind that a roaming ant pays no heed to anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of the ant and that is splits around the first phrase of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inconsiderate person acts thoughtlessly towards other people, without regard for their feelings or needs.
